statement: Nadia's first five quiz scores have a mean of $84$. After her sixth quiz, the mean of all six scores is $86$. What did Nadia score on her sixth quiz?

choices.misconception: I thought the new score had to be the same as the new mean, so I answered 86.
I saw the mean go up by 2 and thought the new score was just 2 more than the new mean, so 86 + 2 = 88.
I said the new score had to give each of the five old scores 2 extra points, but I added those 10 points to the old mean 84 instead of the new mean 86.
I added 2 points for all six scores to the new mean, 86 + 6 times 2 = 98, but the sixth score only has to lift the five old ones.

hints: Think about totals instead of means.
A mean of 84 over five quizzes means the five scores add up to $5 \cdot 84$. What must all six add up to?
The five scores total $5 \cdot 84 = 420$ and the six scores total $6 \cdot 86 = 516$. The sixth score is the difference.

solutions.reliable: The mean times the count is the total. The first five scores total $5 \cdot 84 = 420$. All six scores total $6 \cdot 86 = 516$. So the sixth score is $516 - 420 = 96$.
solutions.elegant: To raise the mean from $84$ to $86$, the sixth score must be $86$ itself plus $2$ extra points for each of the five old scores: $86 + 5 \cdot 2 = 96$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
